description:
FILED s470bm (Opus, 2026-09-05) while recording the `Contract:` docstring tails
for the numeric family (Part B item B1, task #1170).  PRE-EXISTING.

REPRODUCER:

    my ($x, $y) = (1, 0);
    my $r = eval { $x / $y };
    print "err=[$@]\n";

  perl 5.40.3   err=[Illegal division by zero at FILE line 2.]
  PCL           err=[arithmetic error division-by-zero signalled
                     Operation was (/ 1 0). at (eval 0) line 0.]

THE CONTROL FLOW IS RIGHT -- `eval {}` catches it and `$@` is set, so this is
not a correctness bug in the exception model.  What leaks is the TEXT: PCL
lets SBCL's `DIVISION-BY-ZERO` condition print itself, so the message names a
CL form (`Operation was (/ 1 0)`) and carries no perl file/line.  `p-/` has no
`handler-case` at all; the condition reaches the top-level handler that turns
any CL error into a perl-shaped die.

WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING THOUGH ERROR TEXT IS NOT A GOAL (memory:
project_error_message_fidelity_not_required, USER "exact fatal-error TEXT not
a goal unless cheap").  Two reasons:
  1. It is CHEAP -- one `handler-case` on `division-by-zero` in `p-/` (and
     `p-/=` / `p-/=-raw`, which reach the same arithmetic).
  2. It is a HOST LEAK of the kind Part B item B4 is about: a program's
     observable output contains a CL s-expression.  A JS or C backend
     following ir-spec cannot reproduce it, so any test that matches on it is
     unportable by construction, and perl's own t/ has such tests.

The IEEE model is set up for this deliberately -- cl/pcl-runtime.lisp masks
every FP trap at startup EXCEPT `:divide-by-zero`, precisely because perl dies
on `1/0` and `1/0.0`.  So the trap is wanted; only its message is wrong.

RELATED: #1173 is the modulo twin, and worse (it answers NaN instead of dying
at all).  Fix them together: one perl-shaped die each, in the same commit.

BAR: the reproducer; `1/0.0`, `$x /= 0`, and the message's file/line matching
perl's shape; the gate; the full sweep and the op/ companion leg (`cl/`
change).  Read the blessed baselines for rows that match the CL text.

=== DONE (s470bo) ===

FIXED, in the same commit as #1173 as this task asked.  `p-/`'s fast path and
`%p-/-slow`'s fallback both call one inlined `%p-divide-numbers`, which dies
`Illegal division by zero` before dividing; `p-/=` and `p-/=-raw` already
delegate to `p-/`, so the compound spellings came along.  SBCL's own
DIVISION-BY-ZERO condition â and with it the `Operation was (/ 1 0)`
s-expression in a perl program's `$@` â no longer reaches the top-level
handler.

THE ZERO TEST IS ON THE NUMBER, not the truncated number, and that is the one
place `/` and `%` differ.  Probed 5.40.3: `5 / 0.5` is 10 and `1 / -0.0` DIES,
while `5 % 0.5` dies.  Also probed: `1 / "abc"`, `1 / ""` and `1 / undef` all
die (to-number gives 0), and so does `0 / 0`.

Fifteen expressions across the two ops now agree with perl where eight did
not.  The IEEE setup was already right â the runtime masks every FP trap at
startup EXCEPT `:divide-by-zero`, precisely because perl dies on `1/0` â so
only the message was wrong, exactly as this task said.

BARS: as #1173 (one commit).  Two run rows of the six are #1174's:
the message and trappability, and the four other spellings (`1/0.0`, `$x/=0`,
`1/"abc"`, `1/undef`) plus `5/0.5` = 10 in one row.
subject: `1/0` dies with SBCL's own text ("arithmetic error division-by-zero signalled / Operation was (/ 1 0)") - a HOST LEAK in a runtime message, where perl says "Illegal division by zero"
